sections.heading: Core Gameplay Mechanics
sections.body:
Pong Cricket's core gameplay mechanics are simple yet engaging. Players control a paddle to hit a ball back and forth on the screen, trying to score points by hitting the ball into the opponent's goal. The game is played on a small court, with the ball bouncing back and forth at high speeds. The goal is to hit the ball in such a way that it bounces off the opponent's paddle and into the goal.

As the game progresses, the ball moves faster, making it increasingly difficult to control. The opponent's paddle also moves on its own, adding an extra layer of challenge to the game. Players can use their mouse, keyboard, or touch controls to move their paddle left or right, trying to hit the ball at the perfect angle.

One of the unique features of Pong Cricket is the power-ups that appear on the court. These power-ups can give players an edge over their opponents, such as speed boosts, increased paddle size, or even the ability to freeze time. However, players must time their power-up usage carefully, as it can also backfire and give their opponents an advantage.

The core gameplay mechanics of Pong Cricket are easy to learn but difficult to master, making it an ideal choice for players who enjoy a challenge. The game's simple yet engaging concept and fast-paced action will keep players on the edge of their seats, trying to outmaneuver their opponents and emerge victorious.
